title: Temporal: Durable Execution Overview
snippet: Durable execution replays a workflow's history to restore state after a crash. Workers are stateless; the event history in the datastore is the source of truth.

title: Idempotency Keys in Payment APIs
snippet: An idempotency key lets a client safely retry a request. The server stores the key with the first response and returns that same response for any later request carrying the key.

title: Leases and Fencing Tokens
snippet: A lease grants exclusive access for a bounded time. A fencing token is a monotonically increasing number attached to each lease, so a stalled holder's late write is rejected by the storage layer.

title: Exponential Backoff and Jitter
snippet: Full jitter picks a random delay between zero and the exponentially growing cap. Without jitter, clients that fail together retry together and recreate the overload.

title: PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED for Queues
snippet: SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lets many workers pull disjoint rows from a queue table without blocking each other, making Postgres a workable job queue at moderate scale.

title: Redis Streams Consumer Groups
snippet: Consumer groups distribute stream entries across consumers with at-least-once delivery. XAUTOCLAIM reassigns entries that a dead consumer accepted but never acknowledged.

title: The Cost of Large Language Model Tokens
snippet: Providers bill separately for input and output tokens, with output typically five times the input rate. Prompt caching can cut the cost of a repeated prefix by about ninety percent.

title: Two-Phase Commit and Its Limits
snippet: Two-phase commit gives atomicity across participants but blocks when the coordinator fails. Most systems prefer idempotent retries over distributed transactions.

title: Speed of Light in Vacuum
snippet: The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299792458 metres per second, a defined constant since the 1983 redefinition of the metre.

title: Earth to Moon Distance
snippet: The mean distance from Earth to the Moon is about 384400 kilometres, varying between roughly 356500 km at perigee and 406700 km at apogee.
